title.narrative: Empowering the state and municipal institutions and civil society to promote dialogue and a culture of peace

description.narrative: The project will be implemented over a period of 36 months, starting in March 2026 and running until March 2029. The projects primary objective is to foster trust and collaboration between government institutions and civil society in ten cities and districts prone to conflict. This will be achieved through the establishment of inclusive dialogue platforms, the provision of legal support and capacity-building initiatives, and the promotion of participatory governance, social cohesion and human rights. The project supports the localisation of National Action Plans on Social Cohesion and UNSCR 1325, placing a strong emphasis on gender equality and youth engagement. The project will align with national reforms, including the Administrative Territorial Reform, and contribute to the UNSDCF 2023–2027 and SDGs 4, 5, 10, 16 and 17. The project aims to enhance inclusive governance by building partnerships between state and civil society actors, empowering civil society organisations (especially those led by women and young people) to participate meaningfully in public affairs and enabling state institutions to engage constructively. Ultimately, the project envisages a sustainable model of collaboration that reduces polarisation and fosters a culture of peace and mutual trust.

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

The Implementing Partner shall ensure that all of its obligations set forth under the section entitled “Legal Context and/or Risk Management Standard Clauses” are passed on to each responsible party, subcontractor and sub-recipient and that all the clauses under this section entitled “Risk Management” are included, mutatis mutandis, in all sub-contracts or sub-agreements entered into further to the Project Document
